A local research workflow for comparing two frozen image models, recording decisions and preserving traceable evidence. This is not a diagnostic or patient-care tool.

The preparation script generates synthetic images and trains two small PyTorch U-Net models on CPU. These prepared synthetic models demonstrate software mechanics. They do not establish medical accuracy.
Four synthetic images and one intentionally unreadable file were selected in the actual application. Session limits are 500 files, 30 MB per file and 2 GB total. No image-upload service is used.

The created session initially retained four pending images and one input error. Processing is synchronous and bounded. The user can stop between steps and recover an unfinished claim after interruption.

The actual browser run completed four images with two verified models: eight predictions, with one unreadable input retained as an error. This completed-state capture is not a real-time progress recording.
The source image is shown here through the application fullscreen control. Full image context matters: a plausible measurement alone cannot establish that the model located the correct structure.

This is an actual prediction from the selected synthetic seed-43 model. The overlay is generated by the application. Source and label bytes are verified before preview; the same verified bytes are decoded.
This is the second selected model, synthetic seed-42. Disagreement orders cases for inspection. It is not a calibrated probability of error. Models can also agree on the wrong structure.

The demo operator selected held with the reason uncertain. Refreshing the review record retained that decision. This is an AI-operated mechanics demonstration, not clinician approval or independent human checking.

The evidence ZIP was built and downloaded through the actual UI. A separate command-line verifier accepted its six payloads. Default exports exclude images, masks, filenames, local paths and private notes; hashes do not guarantee anonymity.

A separate real-model synthetic audit processed 100 repeated cases plus one unreadable input, retaining 200 predictions after a controlled unfinished claim and recovery. Repeated cases are not independent patients or clinical evidence.
